Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- Advise strict glove use at all times when cleaning to reduce contact with irritants; identify and avoid potential triggers from cleaning products.
- Initiate skin therapy for hand dermatitis with topical corticosteroid cream to affected palms and stronger emollients; apply 3–4 times daily for the next 2 weeks.
  - Note: dose/route/frequency for these medications not documented; prescription to be sent to the patient’s pharmacy.
- Schedule follow-up in 10–14 days (approximately 2 weeks). If symptoms spread, worsen, or do not improve by then, patient should return sooner for reevaluation.
- Provide patient education on skin care and trigger avoidance; reassess treatment efficacy at follow-up.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Soreness and cracking of skin on hands, predominantly palms; associated itching.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms began about 2–4 months ago; currently worse and interfering with work.
- Progression: Worsening over time; pain limits ability to work in housekeeping.
- Aggravating factors: Occupational exposure to cleaning products; inconsistent use of gloves.
- Location: Palms predominantly; some dryness noted on legs.
- Associated symptoms: Itching; occasional bleeding only when scratched.
- Denies fever, nausea/vomiting, bowel or urinary symptoms.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; on metformin.
- Medications: Metformin (dosage not documented).
- Allergies: None.
- Social history: Works as a hotel housekeeper; globe of gloves inconsistent; non-smoker; consumes minimal alcohol (a couple pints per week).
- Family history: Diabetes noted.

Objective:
- Skin findings: Hands dry with cracking, mainly on the palms; itching present.
- Bleeding: Occasional bleeding with scratching; no spontaneous bleeding reported.
- General: Patient appears well; no systemic symptoms reported.
- Other: No other physical exam findings documented.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Dermatitis of the hands (likely contact dermatitis/hand eczema) due to occupational exposure:
   - Assessment: Dermatitis with palm involvement; possible irritant or allergic contact dermatitis considering cleaning-product exposure and inconsistent glove use.
   - Differential diagnoses: Irritant contact dermatitis; allergic contact dermatitis; hand eczema.
   - Investigations planned: None specified.
   - Treatment planned: 
     - Topical corticosteroid cream to affected palms (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Stronger emollients (moisturizers) with frequent application.
     - Education on avoiding triggers and using gloves consistently.
   - Referrals: None indicated at this time.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing elements: Exact medication doses/frequencies for metformin; vitals; detailed physical exam measurements; any prior dermatology history or skin tests.
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional brevity in some responses but sufficient to establish diagnosis and plan.
